4155.t: Originally a Northwest Semitic goddess name from the root כ־ב־ר / ك ب ر (k b r) which is attested as Arabic الْكُبْرَى (al-kubrā, literally “the great”) in a variant reading of Sura 62, Aya 9.

4178.t: From γάμος (gắmos, “marriage; matrimony”) + -έω (-éō, denominative verbal suffix) (though Beekes considers the noun a back-formation from the verb rather than the verb being derived from the noun).

4156.t: Literally, “cunning”, from μήδεα (mḗdea, “cunning, counsels, device, planning”) + -ια (-iă, feminine suffix), from μέδω (médō, “to rule over, protect”), from Proto-Indo-European *med- (“to measure, give advice, heal”).

4108.t: From Proto-Hellenic *ekʰinos, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁eǵʰis (“hedgehog, hedgehog-like animals”). Cognates include Mycenaean Greek 𐀁𐀑𐀜 (e-ki-no), Old Armenian ոզնի (ozni), Proto-Germanic *igilaz, Albanian esh.

4112.t: From Proto-Hellenic *éhər, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁ésh₂r̥. Cognates include Hittite 𒂊𒌍𒄯 (ēšḫar), Sanskrit असृ॑ज् (ásṛj), Old Armenian արիւն (ariwn), Latin sanguis and Old Latin assyr.

4144.t: From Proto-Hellenic *ōmós, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eh₃mós (“raw, bitter, sour”). Cognates include Sanskrit आम (āmá), Old Armenian հում (hum, “raw”), and Irish amh.

4147.t: From Proto-Hellenic *hrutʰmós, corresponding to Proto-Indo-European *sru-dʰ-mo-s, ultimately from *srew- (“to flow”). Related to ῥέω (rhéō, “to flow”).

4175.t: According to Beekes, the word might be of Pre-Greek origin if the connection with the Hesychian gloss βρυγχός (brunkhós) is reliable, which would show an instance of prenasalization.

4185.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *gerbʰ- Proto-Hellenic *grə́pʰō Ancient Greek γράφω (gráphō) Proto-Indo-European *-tós Proto-Hellenic *-tós Ancient Greek -τός (-tós) Ancient Greek γραπτός Verbal adjective of γράφω (gráphō), with suffix -τός (-tós).

4138.t: From ὑπο- (hŭpo-, “hypo-, under-”) + ἐρέτης (erétēs, “rower”), with the suffix ὑπο- (hŭpo-) invoking a sense of opposition to the higher κελευστής (keleustḗs, “boatswain”), rather than one who literally "rows under (a structure, etc.)".

4176.t: A loanword of unknown, possibly Pre-Greek, origin. Perhaps cognate with Hittite 𒆳𒊭𒀸 (kur-ša-aš); see there for more.

4168.t: From αὐτο- (auto-) + κράτωρ (krátōr, “ruler”) (from κρατέω (kratéō, “to rule, command”) and -τωρ (-tōr, “masculine agent suffix.”), from κράτος (krátos, “power, strength”))

4187.t: From the stem of γυμνάζω (gumnázō, “to exercise”), from γυμνός (gumnós, “naked”), and -ιον (-ion), neuter of adjective suffix -ιος (-ios).

4148.t: The word may belong with ῥάβδος (rhábdos, “rod, wand”) and cognates. According to Beekes, it is quite probably a Pre-Greek word.

4191.t: According to Beekes, of Semitic origin, related to dalet. (A connection to delta, ultimately from the same Semitic source, has also been proposed.)

4133.t: From ὁμῶς (homôs, “together; equally, alike”), with stress shift.

4101.t: Unknown, but possibly related to ἔρις (éris, “strife”).

4174.t: According to Beekes, of Pre-Greek origin, based on the alternating ρο/ορ vocalism.

4121.t: As a secondary formation in -ντ- (-nt-), presupposes a noun *ἱμα (*hĭmā) or *ἱμα (*hĭmă) meaning "rope", which is also continued in ἱμάω (hĭmắō), ἱμάσθλη (hĭmắsthlē) and ἱμαῖος (hĭmaîos).

4132.t: From ὀξύς (oxús, “sharp; sour”), with an analogous formation as ἦδος (êdos, “delight, pleasure”) to ἡδύς (hēdús, “pleasant, sweet”).

4104.t: Nominal derivative of ἕννυμι (hénnumi, “to get dressed”).

4103.t: The stem of this word is also found in ἐρύσιμον (erúsimon, “hedge-mustard”) and ἐρυσίπελας (erusípelas, “erysipelas”).

4115.t: From ἐν (en, “in possession of”) + ὅπλον (hóplon, “implements of war”) + -ος (-os, adjectival suffix).

4192.t: From the aorist stem of δάπτω (dáptō, “to devour, consume”), with a suffix in -ιλ-.

4114.t: From ἐκλύω (eklúō, “set free”) + -σις (-sis, “a suffix added to verb stems to form abstract nouns or nouns of action, result or process”)

4118.t: Of unclear origin; not related to ἡμέρα (hēmérā, “day”).

4130.t: ὅρμος (hórmos, “cord, necklace, collar”) + -ίσκος (-ĭ́skos, suffix forming diminutive nouns)
